strategies.name: opening_range_breakout_close_entry
strategies.entry_summary: Define the 15-minute opening range from the 9:30 New York candle high and low. Enter long at the open of the next candle after a candle breaks above the range and closes outside it, with a cutoff of no new trades after the 12:00 candle.
strategies.exit_summary: Place the stop loss at the bottom of the opening range and target 1.5:1 reward-to-risk.

variants.timeframe_note: 15-minute chart; opening range is the 9:30 candle
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for a candle to break out and close above the range, then enter at the next candle open
variants.target_note: 1.5:1 reward-to-risk; stop at bottom of range

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: breakout must be at least 1 times ATR to be considered suitable

variants.transcript_quote: I made sure that this was greater than at least 1 times ATR to be considered a suitable breakout

strategies.name: opening_range_pullback_stop_order_at_range_high
strategies.entry_summary: After the breakout, wait for price to pull back to the opening range and place a stop order at the top of the opening range so entry triggers immediately when price hits that level, rather than waiting for confirmation via a high break.
strategies.exit_summary: Keep the stop loss at the bottom of the opening range and use a 1.5:1 take-profit target.

strategies.name: opening_range_pullback_midpoint_bounce_entry
strategies.entry_summary: Measure the breakout from the top of the opening range, then wait for price to retrace deeper into the range to its midpoint. Enter immediately with a stop order at the midpoint instead of waiting for confirmation of a prior high break.
strategies.exit_summary: Use a smaller stop because entry is at the midpoint; the speaker still frames targets around 1.5:1, with the possibility of aiming for more.

result.enumeration_note: The video teaches four runnable long-only entry/exit skeletons: the speaker's base 15m ORB breakout, a 5m breakout-pullback-continuation confirmation entry, a pullback stop-order-at-range-high variant, and a midpoint pullback stop-order entry. The closing mention about doing the opposite/focusing on momentum is not promoted because no runnable exit rules are taught.
